item.title: Discover the Timeless Art of Crochet with Wedad Kn.: A Journey Through History, Techniques, and Creativity.
item.dc:creator: nemahalsayed
item.content:encoded:
Crochet is more than just a craft—it’s a timeless art form that weaves together history, culture, and creativity. If you’ve ever marveled at the intricate patterns of a crocheted blanket or the delicate beauty of a handmade doily, you’ve witnessed the magic of this centuries-old technique. Today, we’re diving into the world of crochet, exploring its rich history, diverse techniques, and the inspiring work of Wedad Kn., a talented crochet artist whose Instagram account (@Wedadsart) is a must-follow for anyone who loves handmade artistry.

The History and Origin of Crochet

The word crochet comes from the French term croche, meaning "hook," and it’s believed to have originated in the 16th century. While its exact origins are debated, crochet as we know it today gained popularity in Europe during the 19th century. It was often used to create lace-like fabrics, which were highly prized for their beauty and intricacy.

Crochet has deep cultural roots across the globe. From the Irish crochet lace that helped families survive the Great Famine to the vibrant amigurumi toys of Japan, this craft has evolved into a universal language of creativity. It’s a testament to how a simple hook and thread can transform into something extraordinary.

The Art of Crochet: Techniques and Styles

Crochet is a versatile craft with countless techniques and styles. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced crafter, there’s always something new to learn. Here are some popular crochet techniques you’ll find showcased on @Wedadsart Instagram:

  1. Amigurumi: The Japanese art of crocheting small, stuffed toys and figurines. From adorable animals to whimsical characters, amigurumi is a favorite among crochet enthusiasts.
  2. Filet Crochet: A technique that uses open and solid stitches to create intricate lace patterns, often used in doilies, table runners, and decorative pieces.
  3. Tunisian Crochet: A hybrid of knitting and crochet, this technique creates a dense, textured fabric perfect for blankets and scarves.
  4. Granny Squares: A classic crochet motif, granny squares are small, colorful pieces that can be joined to make larger projects like blankets, bags, and even clothing.
  5. Freeform Crochet: A creative and unstructured approach where artists like Wedad Kn combine different stitches and shapes to create unique, one-of-a-kind pieces.

Why Follow Wedad Kn on Instagram?

Wedad Kn is a rising star in the world of crochet, and her Instagram account (@Wedadsart) is a treasure trove of inspiration. Here’s why you should hit that follow button:

  • Stunning Creations: From cozy blankets to intricate lacework, Wedad’s work showcases the beauty and versatility of crochet.
  • Tutorials and Tips: Whether you’re a beginner or an expert, Wedad shares helpful tips and step-by-step tutorials to help you improve your skills.
  • Behind-the-Scenes: Get a glimpse into Wedad’s creative process, from choosing yarns to designing patterns.
  • Community Love: Wedad’s account is a welcoming space for crochet lovers to connect, share ideas, and celebrate the joy of handmade art.

Crochet: A Craft for Everyone

One of the most beautiful things about crochet is its accessibility. All you need is a hook, some yarn, and a little patience to get started. It’s a meditative and rewarding hobby that allows you to create functional art—whether it’s a cozy scarf, a decorative pillow, or a heartfelt gift for a loved one.

By following @Wedadsart on Instagram, you’ll not only discover the endless possibilities of crochet but also support a passionate artist who is keeping this ancient craft alive in the modern world. So, grab your hook, pick up some yarn, and let Wedad Kn inspire your next crochet project!

Follow Wedad Kn. on Instagram (@Wedadsart) today and join a community that celebrates the art, history, and joy of crochet!

item.title: A Taste of Istanbul’s Maritime Heritage: My Kumkapı Balık Pazarı Adventure;
item.dc:creator: nemahalsayed
item.content:encoded:
Nestled along the Marmara Sea in the heart of Istanbul, the Kumkapı Balık Pazarı (Kumkapı Fish Market) is more than just a market—it’s a living testament to the city’s deep connection to the sea. For centuries, this vibrant neighborhood has been a hub for fishermen, merchants, and food lovers, offering some of the freshest seafood in the world. As someone who loves exploring culinary traditions, I couldn’t resist visiting this iconic market during my time in Istanbul.

A Glimpse into History

Kumkapı’s story dates back to the Byzantine era, when it was known as Kontoskalion, a bustling port where fishermen and traders gathered. Over the centuries, it evolved into a thriving fishing district under the Ottomans, home to a diverse community of Greeks, Armenians, and Turks. Today, the market remains a symbol of Istanbul’s maritime heritage, where the scent of the sea mingles with the sounds of lively auctions and the chatter of locals haggling over the day’s catch.

My Kumkapı Experience

During my visit, I was lucky enough to receive a special gift from my friends at the market—a beautiful, fresh fish that reminded me of jewfish. After some research and a closer look at its features, I discovered it was an Orfoz (grouper), a prized fish in Turkish cuisine known for its firm, white flesh and mild flavor. Inspired by its quality, I decided to turn it into sushi, and the result was nothing short of spectacular. The freshness of the fish truly shone through, making it a meal to remember.

Many common fish sold at the Kumkapı Balık Pazarı include:

  • Levrek (Sea Bass): A popular fish in Turkish cuisine, often grilled or baked.
  • Çupra (Sea Bream): Another common fish, similar to sea bass but with a slightly different shape.
  • Palamut (Bonito): A larger, oily fish often used in grilling or curing.
  • Lüfer (Bluefish): A prized fish in Istanbul, especially in autumn, known for its rich flavor.
  • Hamsi (Anchovy): A small, silvery fish, very popular in Black Sea cuisine.
  • İstavrit (Horse Mackerel): A smaller fish, often fried or grilled.

Why Kumkapı Balık Pazarı is a Must-Visit

Kumkapı isn’t just a place to buy fish—it’s an experience. From the early morning auctions to the charming meyhanes (traditional taverns) that line the streets, the market offers a glimpse into Istanbul’s rich culinary culture. Whether you’re a seafood enthusiast or simply curious about local traditions, Kumkapı is a destination that shouldn’t be missed.

A Special Offer for My Viewers

If my story has inspired you to visit Kumkapı Balık Pazarı, I have some exciting news! My friends at the market have generously agreed to offer 10% off to my viewers. Simply mention Nemah of NDesignstudyosu from Syria when you visit, and they’ll be happy to extend this special discount. Trust me, it’s an experience you won’t want to miss!

So, what are you waiting for? Head to Kumkapı, explore the market, and savor the flavors of Istanbul’s maritime heritage. Don’t forget to share your own experiences in the comments—I’d love to hear about your adventures!

I began my tour by visiting the historic Isbank Museum, which was founded by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, the founder of the modern Turkish Republic:

These artistic masterpieces are evidence that the Ottoman language was still in use in 1924.

We continue our tour at the Museum of Art and Civilization, where the highest professional techniques in engineering, design, and banking are combined:

Then I continued my tour to the Hagia Sophia Museum and took many wonderful pictures that testify to the Ottoman craftsmanship in calligraphy, poetry and art, such as this exhibition:

The golden inscription tells us about the castle built by Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror during the blessed month of Ramadan in Constantinople. The last line of the plaque reads, "Exactly 83 AH."

We will quote the verses from another plaque, along with a translation of their meanings:

Hurşid Şevket Şehriyar'ın değiştirilmiş şiirinin başlangıcı

Bani Baniyan Devlet, Kutsal Ev'in hizmetkarı

Milal Sirtah'ın krallığının varisi olan iki genç adam

Azal Dadar İskender Gulam'ın gölgesi süslenmeye devam etti

Dön, Sultan Mustafa sana ihanet etti

Tajdaran Salfadeh Kormade sanki uyuyormuşum gibi

Eliop, Shilshanem'in parasını bozdurdu

Aksa Maram'da yeni bir ev inşa edeceğim

"Bu Diwan Samayoun" cümlesi için özür imzalandı

In today’s fast-paced digital landscape, creativity is the lifeblood of successful marketing. But even the most brilliant minds hit creative blocks. That’s where AI steps in—not to replace marketers, but to supercharge their imagination. With the right prompts, AI tools can become powerful collaborators, helping businesses generate fresh ideas, streamline workflows, and connect more deeply with their audience.

In this post, we’ll explore the most popular AI prompts that marketers are using to boost creativity and drive results. Whether you're crafting campaigns, writing content, or analyzing performance, these prompts will help you unlock new possibilities.

🧠 1. Brand Strategy Prompts

Prompt:

“Generate a unique brand positioning statement for [industry/product].”

Why it works: This prompt helps marketers clarify their brand’s identity and stand out in a crowded market. AI can synthesize competitive insights and customer needs to craft a compelling positioning statement that resonates.

🎯 2. Target Audience Prompts

Prompt:

“Describe the ideal customer persona for [product/service].”

Why it works: Understanding your audience is key to effective marketing. This prompt helps define demographics, pain points, motivations, and buying behaviors—perfect for tailoring your messaging.

📝 3. Content Creation Prompts

Prompt:

“Write 5 engaging blog post titles about [topic] for [audience].”

Why it works: Need fresh content ideas? This prompt sparks creativity and ensures your blog titles are optimized for clicks and relevance.

📣 4. Social Media Prompts

Prompt:

“Create a week’s worth of Instagram captions for [brand/product].”

Why it works: Social media thrives on consistency and creativity. This prompt helps marketers plan ahead with engaging, on-brand content that drives interaction.

📧 5. Email Marketing Prompts

Prompt:

“Write a high-converting email campaign for [offer/event].”

Why it works: From subject lines to CTAs, AI can craft persuasive emails that boost open rates and conversions—saving time while increasing impact.

🔍 6. SEO Optimization Prompts

Prompt:

“Suggest SEO-friendly keywords and meta descriptions for [topic/page].”

Why it works: SEO is both art and science. This prompt helps marketers optimize content for search engines without sacrificing readability.

📈 7. Campaign Ideation Prompts

Prompt:

“Brainstorm 3 creative marketing campaign ideas for launching [product].”

Why it works: Launching something new? This prompt fuels innovative thinking and helps marketers explore angles they might not have considered.

🗣️ 8. Ad Copywriting Prompts

Prompt:

“Write 3 variations of persuasive ad copy for [platform] targeting [audience].”

Why it works: Great ads require testing. This prompt delivers multiple versions of compelling copy, ready for A/B testing and performance optimization.

🎥 9. Video Script Prompts

Prompt:

“Draft a short video script for promoting [product] on TikTok.”

Why it works: Video is king in digital marketing. This prompt helps marketers create snappy, platform-specific scripts that grab attention and drive engagement.

🧪 10. A/B Testing Prompts

Prompt:

“Suggest A/B test variations for [email/ad/landing page].”

Why it works: Optimization is ongoing. This prompt helps marketers experiment with headlines, layouts, and CTAs to find what works best.

🤝 11. Influencer Outreach Prompts

Prompt:

“Write a pitch email to collaborate with influencers in [niche].”

Why it works: Influencer partnerships can amplify reach. This prompt helps marketers craft personalized, professional outreach messages that get noticed.

📊 12. Analytics & Insights Prompts

Prompt:

“Summarize key marketing insights from this campaign data: [paste data].”

Why it works: AI can quickly analyze performance data and highlight trends, helping marketers make informed decisions without drowning in spreadsheets.

item.title: Building a Sharia‑Compliant Banking System with PostgreSQL: A Deep Dive into Modern Islamic Finance Engineering
item.dc:creator: nemahalsayed
item.content:encoded:
Islamic finance is one of the fastest‑growing sectors in global banking — yet high‑quality, open‑source systems that model real Sharia‑compliant workflows are rare. To bridge that gap, I built a Sharia‑Compliant Banking Management System (SCBMS): a fully structured PostgreSQL backend that models Islamic banking operations with accuracy, automation, and transparency.

This post walks through the key ideas behind the project, the architecture, and some of the SQL powering it.

🌐 Why Build a Sharia‑Compliant Banking System?

Islamic finance operates on principles fundamentally different from conventional banking:

  • No interest (riba)
  • No uncertainty (gharar)
  • No prohibited activities
  • Profit‑loss sharing
  • Asset‑backed financing

Designing a system that respects these rules requires more than tables — it requires business logic, automation, and auditability.

That’s where PostgreSQL shines.

🏗️ System Architecture at a Glance

The system is built using a layered architecture that mirrors real banking backends:

Database Layer

  • customers
  • accounts
  • transactions
  • murabahacontracts
  • ijaracontracts
  • mudarabainvestments
  • zakatcalculations

Stored Procedures

  • calculate_zakat()
  • generate_murabaha_payment_plan()
  • generate_ijara_schedule()

Triggers

  • audit_prohibited_transactions
  • update_account_balance

Views

  • CustomerPortfolioView
  • ZakatSummaryView

Future API Layer

  • REST endpoints
  • authentication
  • business logic services

This structure makes the system scalable, maintainable, and ready for integration with Python, Node.js, or a full web application.

Example: Creating a Customer and Opening Accounts

Here’s a simple SQL snippet that demonstrates how the system handles customer onboarding:

INSERT INTO islamic_finance.customers
(full_name, national_id_or_passport, date_of_birth, customer_type, email, phone_number, zakat_eligible)
VALUES
('Demo User', 'A123456789', '1990-01-01', 'Individual', 'demo@example.com', '555-1234', TRUE)
RETURNING customer_id;

Automating Murabaha Financing

Murabaha is a cost‑plus financing model where the bank buys an asset and sells it to the customer at a profit.

The system includes a stored procedure that automatically generates the payment schedule:

CALL islamic_finance.generate_murabaha_payment_plan(1, 6);

Real‑Time Shariah Compliance with Triggers

Triggers enforce rules automatically:

  • audit_prohibited_transactions logs any suspicious activity
  • update_account_balance keeps balances accurate
  • log_shariah_violations ensures transparency

This mirrors how real Islamic banks maintain compliance.

Bonus: Python Integration

To demonstrate full‑stack capability, the project includes a small Python script that connects to PostgreSQL and runs queries:

cur.execute('SET search_path TO islamic_finance, public;')
cur.execute('SELECT full_name, email FROM customers LIMIT 5;')

Final Thoughts

This project is more than a database — it’s a complete Islamic banking backend, built with:

  • Clean architecture
  • Real business logic
  • Automated compliance
  • Expandability for future APIs

It demonstrates how modern engineering can support ethical, Sharia‑compliant financial systems.

If you’re exploring Islamic finance, backend engineering, or database architecture, this project is a powerful foundation to build on.

Here is my github project link:

https://github.com/NemahAlsayed/Sharia-Compliant-Banking-Management-System-SCBMS-

To request any project ideas from me in open source SQL, please contact me. I do technology related blog posts. I post the source code on Github.

What Is WhatConverts?
